html:
The Djiboutian Civil War was an uprising from 1991 to 1994 by an Afar rebel group, the Front for the Restoration of Unity and Democracy, against the Issa-led government of Hassan Gouled Aptidon.

The Afar of the north felt shut out of power since independence. The rebels took much of the north and besieged towns around Tadjoura before the army, with French support, pushed them back.

Under pressure the government accepted a new constitution allowing more parties in 1992, and a peace deal in 1994 brought part of the rebel movement into government, with a final agreement in 2001. The split between Afar and Issa, set in the colonial years, still marks politics in Djibouti.
sum: The Djiboutian Civil War was an uprising from 1991 to 1994 by an Afar rebel group, the Front for the Restoration of Unity and Democracy, against the Issa-led government of Hassan Gouled Aptidon.
